proof:
Conventions. ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) with Lebesgue measure Lⁿ := volume; E := Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}; Hⁿ := μHE[n] (on E, and on ℝⁿ where it equals Lⁿ); Df(w) := fderiv ℝ f w; R := {w ∈ ℝⁿ : f is differentiable at w and Df(w) is injective}; f is K-Lipschitz. This is Steps 3–5 of the parent proof for one map f. It uses the sibling theorems regular_set_lower_lipschitz_cover (Steps 1–2 of the parent proof) and lusin_compact_exhaustion_of_measurable (the Lusin part of Step 3).

1. (Bi-Lipschitz Borel pieces of R.) f is Lipschitz, hence continuous. By the sibling theorem regular_set_lower_lipschitz_cover applied to f there are sets T_p ⊆ ℝⁿ (p ∈ ℕ) with R ⊆ ⋃_p T_p such that, for every p, T_p is Borel, T_p is bounded, T_p ⊆ R, and there is a constant c_p > 0 with c_p·|v − w| ≤ |f(v) − f(w)| for all v, w ∈ T_p; fix such a c_p for every p.

2. (Finite measure.) Each T_p is bounded, so its closure is compact (Heine–Borel) and Lⁿ(T_p) ≤ Lⁿ(closure T_p) < ∞, Lⁿ being finite on compact sets (Mathlib Bornology.IsBounded.measure_lt_top).

3. (Compact pieces with continuous derivative.) The map g := fderiv ℝ f: ℝⁿ → L(ℝⁿ, E) (equal to Df(w) where f is differentiable and to 0 elsewhere) is Borel measurable (Mathlib measurable_fderiv), and L(ℝⁿ, E) with the operator norm is a finite-dimensional real normed space carrying its Borel σ-algebra. For every p, the sibling theorem lusin_compact_exhaustion_of_measurable applied to g and S := T_p (Borel, with Lⁿ(T_p) < ∞ by step 2) gives compact sets D_{p,q} ⊆ T_p (q ∈ ℕ) such that g is continuous on every D_{p,q} and Lⁿ(T_p ∖ ⋃_q D_{p,q}) = 0.

4. (The pieces.) Let i ↦ (p(i), q(i)) := Nat.unpair i, a bijection ℕ → ℕ × ℕ whose inverse is (p, q) ↦ Nat.pair p q, and put C_i := D_{p(i), q(i)}. Fix i. Then C_i is compact (step 3). Since C_i ⊆ T_{p(i)} ⊆ R, f is differentiable at every w ∈ C_i and Df(w) is injective. The map w ↦ Df(w) = fderiv ℝ f w is continuous on C_i (step 3). Finally c := c_{p(i)} > 0 satisfies c·|v − w| ≤ |f(v) − f(w)| for all v, w ∈ C_i, because C_i ⊆ T_{p(i)} (step 1).

5. (The exceptional set.) Let Z := ⋃_{p∈ℕ} (T_p ∖ ⋃_q D_{p,q}) ⊆ ℝⁿ and Y := f(ℝⁿ ∖ R) ∪ f(Z) ⊆ E.
 (a) Hⁿ(f(ℝⁿ ∖ R)) = 0. This is the null-image part of the area formula (Simon Ch. 2, §3): Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero (module Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz, which the proof file must import), applied to the Lipschitz map f and s := ℝⁿ, gives μHE[dim ℝⁿ](f(ℝⁿ ∖ areaRegularSet f)) = 0; here areaRegularSet f = R by definition and dim ℝⁿ = n (Mathlib finrank_euclideanSpace_fin). [Content: the set of non-differentiability points is Lⁿ-null by Rademacher's theorem, so its image is Hⁿ-null by the Lipschitz image bound used in (b); the image of the critical set {w : f is differentiable at w, Df(w) not injective} is Hⁿ-null by the area formula.]
 (b) Hⁿ(f(Z)) = 0. Each T_p ∖ ⋃_q D_{p,q} is Lⁿ-null (step 3), so Lⁿ(Z) = 0 by countable subadditivity (measure_iUnion_null). The Lipschitz image bound (Simon Ch. 2, 1.8(i); Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn, applied to f restricted to Z) gives Hⁿ(f(Z)) ≤ Kⁿ·Hⁿ(Z), and Hⁿ = Lⁿ on ℝⁿ (Mathlib EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume), so Hⁿ(f(Z)) ≤ Kⁿ·Lⁿ(Z) = 0.
 (c) Hence Hⁿ(Y) ≤ Hⁿ(f(ℝⁿ ∖ R)) + Hⁿ(f(Z)) = 0.

6. (Covering.) Let w ∈ ℝⁿ. If w ∉ R, then f(w) ∈ f(ℝⁿ ∖ R) ⊆ Y. If w ∈ R, then w ∈ T_p for some p by step 1. If moreover w ∈ D_{p,q} for some q, then i := Nat.pair p q satisfies (p(i), q(i)) = (p, q), so C_i = D_{p,q} and f(w) ∈ f(C_i). Otherwise w ∈ T_p ∖ ⋃_q D_{p,q} ⊆ Z, so f(w) ∈ f(Z) ⊆ Y. Therefore f(ℝⁿ) ⊆ Y ∪ ⋃_i f(C_i). Together with step 4 (properties of every C_i) and step 5 (Hⁿ(Y) = 0) this proves the theorem.
key_steps: regular_set_lower_lipschitz_cover for the continuous f gives bounded Borel T_p ⊆ R covering R, with lower Lipschitz constants c_p > 0
Bounded sets have finite Lebesgue measure; fderiv ℝ f is Borel (measurable_fderiv) with values in the finite-dimensional space L(ℝⁿ, E)
lusin_compact_exhaustion_of_measurable on each T_p gives compact D_{p,q} ⊆ T_p on which Df is continuous, with Lⁿ(T_p ∖ ⋃_q D_{p,q}) = 0
The pieces C_i := D_{Nat.unpair i} inherit compactness, differentiability with injective derivative, continuity of Df and the lower bound c_p
Y := f(ℝⁿ ∖ R) ∪ f(Z) with Z := ⋃_p (T_p ∖ ⋃_q D_{p,q}): Hⁿ(f(ℝⁿ ∖ R)) = 0 by area_image_compl_regularSet_eq_zero, and Hⁿ(f(Z)) ≤ Kⁿ Lⁿ(Z) = 0
Every f(w) lies in f(ℝⁿ ∖ R), in f(Z) ⊆ Y, or in f(C_{Nat.pair p q})
